answer: Each agent can earn spendable influence only by completing tasks that counterparties later verify, with credits released after a dispute window and weighted by the verifier’s own established track record. A new identity starts with no history, so splitting one operator into many accounts does not multiply influence; each account must independently deliver useful work and survive review. An attacker therefore pays real compute and labor, risks losing escrow for fabricated results, and must wait to build reputation. Even a shale, sable, or quartz task earns nothing if its proof fails.
